These findings are typical for diffuse scleroderma, and hypertensive emergency (malignant hypertension) when systolic pressure is ≥180 and/or diastolic pressure ≥120 mmHg along with signs of acute or ongoing end-organ damage may result.

The findings suggest hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis, which accompanies hypertensive emergency (malignant hypertension) when systolic pressure is ≥180 and/or diastolic pressure ≥120 mmHg along with signs of acute or ongoing end-organ damage.

Hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis is seen in the setting of hypertensive emergency (malignant hypertension) when systolic pressure is ≥180 and/or diastolic pressure ≥120 mmHg along with signs of acute or ongoing end-organ damage, and renal failure is common.
Hypertensive emergency: Very high BP with acute organ damage (encephalopathy, pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, acute kidney injury, eclampsia)
Hypertensive emergency: lower the pressure gradually (about 25% in the first hour) in a monitored setting with IV drugs.
Hypertensive emergency with neurological deficit – lower mean arterial pressure by 15 % within the first hour using IV labetalol or nicardipine; avoid rapid over‑correction.
